note: Reconstruction tables for Classical Chinese, the user's own hypothesis of how a rime-book placement sounds. The initial table gives the onset of every initial the rime books name. The final table gives the final of every rime, keyed by the rime, a space and the division, with a space and 合 appended for the rounded medial; a rime with a 重紐 letter is looked up as written and then without the letter. The tone table splits each rime-book tone into the classes of the reconstruction, one row per class in order: onset is a pattern matched against the onset the initial table gave, the first row whose pattern matches wins, and a row without onset matches every onset; rewrite lists rules run over the whole syllable, onset and final joined; class names the tone class the reading view prints after the reading, 1 to 8 with S for the sonorant split of 上 and 入. Onsets starting p t c s k ʔ h are voiceless, b d q z g x voiced obstruents, m n j w l sonorants. 平 gives 1 to voiceless and 2 to every voiced onset, and unfolds a voiced obstruent into the aspirated voiced series the pack otherwise folds, so 並 reads b in the table and bh under 平; 匣 x has no such series. 上 adds the glottal stop after the coda and gives 3, 4S or 4; 去 adds h and gives 5 or 6; 入 turns a nasal coda into a stop and gives 7, 8S or 8. The reading view prints the reading and the class before the placement, such as /ngoʔ/ 4성S 疑 模[模] 一等 上. This file is kept apart from source.json so the system can grow on its own.
